verdict: GE Vernova's revenue jumped 22% to $11.1B as orders rose 88% organically to $24.2B and the backlog reached $176B, producing $649M of profit — and management raised full-year guidance.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue of $11.1B, up from $9.1B a year ago; +12% organically, led by Power and Electrification

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Up from $1.86 a year ago; net income was $649M, a 5.8% margin

kpis.label: Backlog
kpis.note: Orders of $24.2B in the quarter, +88% organically; backlog grew $13B in three months

kpis.label: Electrification revenue
kpis.note: +68% as reported (+29% organically) — grid equipment is booming, helped by the Prolec GE acquisition

segments.name: Power
segments.note: Gas turbines and other power-plant equipment and services — the biggest business. Revenue +14% on Gas Power equipment; gas equipment backlog plus slot reservations reached 116 GW.

segments.name: Electrification
segments.note: Grid equipment — substations, transformers and high-voltage gear that move electricity. Revenue +68% as reported, including Prolec GE; +29% organically.

segments.name: Wind
segments.note: Wind turbines, onshore and offshore, plus servicing. Revenue -10% on lower onshore equipment deliveries, and the segment lost $275M at the EBITDA level.

segments.name: Other/eliminations
segments.note: Other revenues minus sales between GE Vernova's own segments, removed so the segments add up to the company total.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, offices and running the company.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing new turbines, grid and energy-transition technology — about $0.3B funded in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Orders nearly doubled
takeaways.text: Orders rose 88% organically to $24.2B, driven by Power equipment, and total backlog grew $13B in one quarter to $176B. Gas Power equipment backlog plus slot reservation agreements rose from 100 GW to 116 GW, and the company now expects at least 125 GW under contract by year-end 2026.

takeaways.title: Grid gear is the growth star
takeaways.text: Electrification revenue jumped 68% to $3.6B (+29% without the Prolec GE acquisition) as utilities buy substations and transmission gear, while Power revenue rose 14% to $5.5B. Wind was the drag: revenue fell 10% and the segment EBITDA loss widened to $275M.

takeaways.title: Cash poured in, guidance went up
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $5.1B in the quarter — more than all of 2025 — lifting the cash balance to $13.1B. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $45.5–$46.5B of revenue and $11.5–$12.5B of free cash flow.

oneTimers: Restructuring charges of $9M and separation costs of $38M (from the spin-out from GE) were excluded from adjusted EBITDA of $1,250M, as were $48M of losses on purchases and sales of business interests.
Cost of equipment includes a $35M fair-value adjustment to Prolec GE inventory. GE Vernova bought the remaining 50% of Prolec GE in February 2026 for about $5.3B of cash.
GE Vernova monetized its remaining ownership stake in China XD Electric for about $0.6B of pre-tax proceeds, and voluntarily contributed about $0.5B to the GE Energy Pension Plan.
otherDetail: Other income of $272M is made up of $73M of interest and other financial income, $119M of non-operating benefit income (pension and retiree-benefit plans), and $80M of other income — net. That $80M includes $28M of net interest and investment income (including a $13M gain on selling the remaining China XD stake), $22M of gains on purchases and sales of business interests, $7M of equity-method income, $9M of licensing income and $14M of other items, less $2M of derivative losses (components total $78M; $2M rounding in the filing).
footerNote: GE Vernova reports in whole $ millions; cost of revenue is the filing's $8,744M total and SG&A carries a $1M rounding plug so the lines add up exactly.
